solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: B closely paraphrases P5 ('for years I had never let him have it'), but it is a main-idea item, so restating the turning point is reasonable
minor: overlaps conceptually with R036-02 and R036-04 (all about softened translation); none gives away another's key
R036-01.notes: The core of the story: the narrator's smoothing kept the father from ever hearing, and answering, the real words. D tempts readers who assume a resolution, but the narrator never decides to stop translating. A and C are not supported.

flags: minor: answer cue - D paraphrases the very next clause ('taking the jolts out of every conversation before they reached the other side'), so this is nearly a lookup
minor: B (absorbing blame) is a weak distractor
R036-02.notes: Both examples show softening in both directions. C ('stopped conversations') is the main trap, because the conversations continued.

flags: minor: B and C are weak distractors that few will pick; D (literal 'not paid') is the only real trap
R036-03.notes: He spoke like someone already owed the thing he asked for, as in calling the bill 'a theft'.

flags: minor: P5 states the reason almost outright ('the sentence I would have wanted to hear'); A, B and D have no support and nobody would pick them
R036-04.notes: The narrator hears that the first attempt softened what the teacher said.

flags: Support for A is inferential: the narrator's age at the conference is never stated ('By the time I was twelve' sets only a lower bound; the small chair hints at youth), and 'a role meant for an adult' relies on reading Ms. Pruitt's request for 'an interpreter' as expecting a professional or an adult. Defensible as the best answer, but a key note should cite this evidence.
minor: D is a plausible trap - the teacher may well have known the narrator would come, though the text does not say so
R036-05.notes: The terse sentence contrasts the formal request for 'an interpreter' with the reality: the child does it. B (resentment) is not in the tone, and C is unsupported.

flags: minor: A and C contradict P7 outright, so the distractors are weak; borderline easy/medium
R036-06.notes: The narrator braced for 'sharpness'; instead the father laughed and thanked the teacher.

R036-07.notes: Tomas 'treats every conversation as if it belongs to him', which echoes the father's blunt way of making requests. C ('smart') is the main trap; D has a little appeal.

R036-08.notes: 'Telling him straight' means telling him honestly or directly. A is a mild trap.

flags: minor: D has some pull, because the narrator 'did not translate right away' after the father laughed; but the father laughed in surprise, not 'at Ms. Pruitt's remarks', and the narrator's reply ('trying to get it right') points to A. One defensible answer.
R036-09.notes: This refers to the slower translating with pauses in P6, which the father noticed. B and C are unsupported.
